description: The puzzle build demo: which puzzle, where the base goes, how each piece is gripped. Positions are in the cell's world frame: metres, z = 0 on the bench top, the rail along x, the table toward -y. Grasps are in each piece's own CAD frame.

survey.what: Wrist D415 straight down, gripper closed. The camera always sees its own gripper: it fills the top middle of the picture and the fingertips end at the picture's centre, so the point looked at is just on the robot's side of the base in the middle, and nothing of the base is hidden.

scan.what: The scan step's views after the survey's own (straight down, the view the matcher reads): where the wrist camera is and the point it looks at. The depth of every view is compared with the matched pieces, which is what tells a piece's rival poses apart. Five frames a view, the number the matcher reads. The picture stays upright in every view (its right as near the world's x as the view allows); for that the arm unwinds wrist 3 from 106 degrees at the left view to -154 at the right one. With the right view a quarter turn round, wrist 3 stayed between 101 and 141 degrees, but only 36 to 200 pixels of each piece were then compared there (over 1000 upright) and the view lined up twenty times worse.

base_check.what: The fast check of the base while a piece is brought to it (scripts/puzzle_base_check.py): one depth picture of the wrist camera at the pre-place hover and after every descent_step_m of lowering, fitted with the base's CAD from its last pose. The camera rides on the gripper and looks along it: a piece that goes in with the gripper level (the forks) is checked once instead, from look_height_m above the base, before it is carried in, and not again. A base found more than moved_mm or moved_deg away, by a fit that is trusted, takes its slots and seated pieces with it and the rest of the placement is laid out again and simulated ahead; at most corrections times per placement. A fit that is not trusted, or other pieces not where they were, puts the piece back and scans the table.

base_target.what: The middle of the table. The yaw puts the forks' slots across the rail, so each fork is brought in from its own side with the gripper level; the base may also arrive half a turn round.

grip_force_source: The lab's RG2 driver (RISL_onrobot_ros, custom_libraries/onrobot.py) sends force_val=400, in units of 0.1 N, with every move: 40 N, the RG2's maximum (datasheet: 3 to 40 N). Not measured on the real gripper.

base3.what: The centre island between the two bar slots, across its 23.1 mm width; the fingertips stand in the bar slots. The island is 7 mm high, enough to slide the plate on the table and not to lift it.

line_brown.what: Across the bar's 25.9 mm width at its middle, the pads' lower edge 7.5 mm above the face the bar lies on: with the bar on the slot floor that is 0.5 mm above the 7 mm slot walls.

fork_orange.what: The centre tab across its 21 mm width, from the fork's flat side: the fork is picked lying flat and turned upright in the hand, and goes into its slot with the gripper level.

corrected_from_table.what: The pieces whose place --correction table shifts by the table's entry for their type (scripts/puzzle_build_corrections.json); a measuring run (--write-corrections) rehearses exactly these. The forks: picked lying flat by the tab and turned upright in the hand, they sit 1.5 to 6.5 mm from the grasp as defined. Not the bars: a bar sits 0.4 to 3.4 mm off in no steady direction, a correction lowers the gripper (the arm hangs about 1 mm low at the pick, so the pads hold the bar lower than defined), and the bar's grasp leaves the pads only 0.5 mm above the slot's walls. With the bars corrected too the build seated 18 of 24 pieces over six layouts, against 23 of 24 without (2026-11-17).

table_camera.what: A second camera for the video only: any camera on a tripod beyond the table's far edge. Off unless --table-camera is given; drawn on the stage for the run, not part of the ur5e-workcell pack, and no step of the build reads it.
